caption: AND with real signal inputs: a torch stands on each input block, so each goes out when its input turns on; the dust between them is then off exactly when both inputs are on, and the wall torch hanging under that dust turns it back into AND. 4 gt, 5 blocks.

NOT gate, 1 block: a wall torch hanging on the input block itself. The input powers that block, the torch goes out, and the torch is the output: lit exactly when the input is off. A row of them side by side inverts a whole bus.

NAND gate, 2 blocks: a wall torch hanging on each input block, and the output lamp touching both torches. Each torch goes out when its own input is on, so the lamp stays lit unless BOTH inputs are on.
OR gate, 1 block, instant: a dust lying on input B's block points into the output, and input A's block sits right beside the output too. Either powered input block lights the output, with no delay.

NOR gate, 2 blocks: a dust lying on input B's block points into input A's block, so A's block is powered whenever A or B is on; the wall torch hanging on A's block is the output, lit only while both are off.

NIMPLY gate (A and not B), 3 blocks: a subtract comparator reads input A's block behind it, and a dust lying ON input B's block sits at its side; the comparator passes A minus B, so the output lights only while A is on and B is off. B's block is the dust's floor.

NIMPLY gate (B and not A), 3 blocks: the mirror of gate-nimply. A subtract comparator reads input B's block behind it, and a dust lying ON input A's block sits at its side, so the output lights only while B is on and A is off.

IMPLY gate (A implies B), 2 blocks, glitch-free: the output lamp sits above a wall torch hanging on input A's block (lit while A is off) and in front of a repeater that stands ON A's block and carries input B (a repeater ignores the block under it). Torch and repeater both take 2 ticks, so switching both inputs at once never blinks the output.

IMPLY gate (B implies A), 2 blocks, glitch-free: the mirror of gate-imply. The output lamp sits above a wall torch hanging on input B's block and in front of a repeater that stands ON B's block and carries input A; both take 2 ticks, so the output never blinks.

XOR gate, 15 blocks, 2 ticks, glitch-free: a dust lies on each input block, and two subtract comparators stand in a square with them, so each dust is one comparator's back and the other's side. The comparator reading A's dust from behind has B's dust at its side and lights only when A is on alone; the other one, the mirror, lights only when B is on alone. The first points straight into the output; the second powers a block whose dust climbs over the square, across stones laid on the core, and lands on top of the output.

XNOR gate, 17 blocks, 4 ticks: the 15-block XOR (a dust on each input block, two subtract comparators in a square with them) whose two signals meet on a stone instead of the output; a wall torch on that stone is the output, lit unless exactly one input is on.
